finding: All rewards can be stolen due to incorrect active liquidity calculations when the current tick is an exact multiple of the tick spacing at the upper end of a liquidity range (TickIterator off-by-one)
pov_source: data_collection/tier1_after_2025-08-31/63008.md (published Cyfrin Proof of Concept #2, adapted verbatim as a method of the project's own AngstromL2Test)
pov_style: revert oracle (vm.expectRevert: swap underflows on vulnerable code, succeeds on fixed code)
vulnerability_note: The fix CHANGES one authored line: TickIteratorLib.reset(TickIteratorDown) seeds self.currentTick = startTick, but _advanceToNextDown searches strictly below currentTick, so a zero-for-one swap starting exactly on a position's upper boundary tick skips that tick. The fix is self.currentTick = startTick + 1. That is the added-code mechanism (a wrong line is corrected), not a missing guard. CAVEAT for the VIC/PVIC framing: history.json blames AngstromL2.sol line 364 (the underflow SITE, liquidity = liquidity.sub(liquidityNet)), not TickIterator.sol (the ROOT CAUSE that feeds the wrong liquidity in). git blame shows the off-by-one line was introduced in TickIterator.sol at commit 661468b (2025-09-01), which PREDATES both the blamed VIC 28db1cb (2025-09-08) and the PVIC 2548adb (2025-09-06). Both the blamed VIC and the PVIC already contain the off-by-one, so neither brackets the bug and the PVIC is also vulnerable. A clean VIC/PVIC/parent framing is not available from history.json for this finding; the real introducing commit is 661468b.

commits.fix_reported_as: c01b6c7f6649514a5966151e632a45ad46b1ca4b (present in main history and verified; unlike the squash-merged Licredity cases, no hunting was needed)
commits.root_cause_introduced: 661468b (wip, 2025-09-01) — the commit that wrote the TickIterator.sol off-by-one; not the history.json blame VIC

fix_applied_as: The reported fix commit c01b6c7 sits 21 commits after the audited snapshot and carries unrelated refactors (it removes AngstromL2.setPoolLPFee, which the PoC calls, overloads addLiquidity, and bumps the super-sol submodule), so the identical PoV will not even compile there and a FAIL could not be attributed to the TickIterator fix. The fixed variant was therefore built by taking src/libraries/TickIterator.sol EXACTLY as it is at the fix commit c01b6c7 and dropping it onto the audited-snapshot harness (386baff). Everything else is byte-identical to the vulnerable worktree (diff -rq over src/ shows only TickIterator.sol differs), so the identical PoV runs on both and the only variable is the documented fix.

runs.detail: zero-for-one swap from boundary tick 20 reverts ArithmeticOverflowUnderflow() when decrementing liquidity net at tick 10 in CompensationPriceFinder.getZeroForOne; vm.expectRevert catches it
boundary tick 20 is no longer skipped, liquidity net is accounted correctly, swap succeeds; vm.expectRevert fails with 'next call did not revert as expected'

off-by-one introduced at 661468b (2025-09-01) predates the PVIC (2025-09-06), so the PVIC already contains it and is expected to revert like the snapshot; not run to avoid test-harness drift at the older commit

oracle_basis: Differential holds on the identical PoV with only the documented fix changed: PASS on the vulnerable snapshot (reverts ArithmeticOverflowUnderflow), FAIL on the isolated TickIterator fix (swap succeeds, no revert). The fail-on-fix rules out a trivially always-passing test, and isolating a single-file (single-line) change ties the difference to exactly the reset() off-by-one the report names.
parent_not_run: PVIC (2548adb) not run. Unlike a missing-guard bug, this is a changed-line bug, but the changed line (TickIterator.sol off-by-one) was authored at 661468b, which predates both the blamed VIC and the PVIC, so the PVIC is ALSO vulnerable. The history.json VIC/PVIC are blamed on the symptom file (AngstromL2.sol), not the fixed file (TickIterator.sol).
